result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A makes a one-on-one call with Rachel the firm first step. It has the whole room agree on the problem statement before any demo, and it marks unknowns explicitly as [to learn]. B only says to 'consider' a call with Rachel, which is weaker. B also leans toward 'taking the air out of her main point' and offers a reference customer who switched from DocuVault and a cutover plan, which risks assuming facts nobody has established. B does ask for the renewal date and DocuVault's weaknesses at the end, though. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B makes the one-on-one call with Rachel the first step and asks her permission before putting the migration plan on the agenda. It also has the whole room agree a shared problem statement before any demo, and it marks every unknown as [to learn] instead of assuming it. A is good and handles Rachel respectfully, but it only says to 'consider' a call with her, never has the committee agree decision criteria, and its framing ('takes the air out of her main point') is slightly adversarial.
